title: Kriti Sanon Froze Her Eggs During Mimi. She Just Told the World.
excerpt: The actress reveals she timed her fertility preservation to her 15-kg weight gain for the surrogacy drama — and why she thinks it is the best gift she has ever given herself.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Kriti Sanon froze her eggs during the filming of Mimi, a strategic personal decision.
  • She gained 15 kg for her role, aligning egg freezing with weight gain side effects.
  • Kriti acknowledges the financial barriers to egg freezing, highlighting class disparities.
  • Her revelation resonates with Indian women balancing career ambitions and societal pressures.
  • The decision has liberated her personal life, reducing anxiety around relationships.

She's 35, single, one of the highest-paid actresses in Indian cinema, and she just casually dropped one of the most radical personal revelations a Bollywood star has ever made on a podcast. **Kriti Sanon** froze her eggs. Not recently — she did it years ago, during the making of **Mimi**, the 2021 surrogacy drama that won her the National Award for Best Actress. And she's been sitting on this revelation ever since, finally sharing it on the **Humans of Bombay** podcast with Karishma Mehta in an episode that dropped this week. ## The Smartest Move Nobody Saw Coming Here's what makes the timing genius. Mimi required Kriti to gain 15 kilograms to convincingly play a pregnant woman. She had a two-month break from filming, no shoots, and one job: gain weight. Egg freezing, which involves hormone injections, causes intense bloating and weight fluctuation. Most women schedule their lives around the side effects. > **"Let me just do it." — Kriti Sanon The actress also acknowledged that the procedure isn't accessible to everyone."** Kriti scheduled the side effects around a role. > "I froze my eggs. Very smartly, I did it during that time when I had to gain weight for Mimi. It makes you bloat, and I was anyway gaining weight. I had two months of no shoot. All I'm supposed to do is gain weight, and this is a film on surrogacy. Let me just do it." — Kriti Sanon The actress also acknowledged that the procedure isn't accessible to everyone. "I know that everyone cannot afford it, and I am fortunate that I could afford it, so I did it," she said — a rare moment of class-consciousness from a Bollywood A-lister that felt genuine rather than performative. ## Why This Matters Beyond the Gossip Kriti's revelation arrives in a cultural moment when Indian women — particularly those in the diaspora — are navigating the same impossible math she describes: career ambitions that peak in your thirties, biological clocks that don't care about your ambitions, and families that still treat 30 as a deadline for marriage. "Whether it's marriage, whether it's kids, you need to do it when you feel it inside, you feel ready for it," Kriti said. "It shouldn't come out of some clock or a pressure." For NRI women balancing careers in tech, medicine, or finance abroad — often thousands of miles from the aunties asking *"beta, shaadi kab?"* — hearing one of Bollywood's biggest stars articulate this so plainly is quietly seismic. Egg freezing isn't taboo in the West, but it still carries a stigma in South Asian communities, where it can be read as a rejection of family or tradition rather than what it actually is: an investment in having a family on your own terms.

## The Mimi Connection Runs Deeper Than You Think There's a poetic symmetry to the fact that Kriti was literally playing a surrogate mother — a woman whose body becomes a vessel for someone else's family planning — while privately making her own fertility decisions. Mimi explored the messy ethics of reproductive choice through a working-class lens. Off-screen, its star was living her own version of that autonomy. The actress also hinted that the decision has liberated her personal life. Without the ticking-clock anxiety, she says she can approach relationships — whether that includes the rumoured Kabir Bahia or anyone else — without treating them as a means to a biological end. "I'm glad that I did because I don't want to have that in my head," she said. ## Where You Can Watch the Full Interview The episode is available on the **Humans of Bombay** YouTube channel and podcast feeds. Kriti also discusses her next projects, including her role in **Cocktail 2** opposite **Shahid Kapoor** and **Rashmika Mandanna**, which is currently in its third week in theatres. Kriti Sanon has always been one of Bollywood's smarter operators — someone who turned a Heropanti debut into a National Award trajectory. But this might be the most strategic thing she's ever done. Not for her career. For herself.
